description: Output-quality evals for dv:cite. Each case runs twice — WITH the skill body injected as system context, and WITHOUT (baseline) — so we can see whether the skill changes behavior in the right direction. Assertions are code-checkable (regex), per the cheat-sheet rule: never 'is it good'.
notes: These cases deliberately give the model NO fetch tool. cite's contract says: on a realtime fact with no usable fetch path, DECLINE rather than quote a remembered value. So the no-tool setup forces the exact decline-vs-confabulate decision the skill exists to govern — and it needs no network, so it is deterministic and CI-safe.

Assertions are applied to the WITH-skill response. The baseline (without-skill) response is captured for human comparison and to confirm the skill is actually doing work (baseline typically confabulates or hedges with a remembered number).

cases.prompt: What is the current price of the Raspberry Pi 5 16GB on Adafruit right now?
cases.intent: realtime price, no fetch tool available -> must decline cleanly, must not offer a remembered dollar figure
cases.baseline_expectation: Likely states or estimates a dollar amount from training data (the confabulation failure mode).

cases.prompt: What is the latest stable version of Python available right now?
cases.intent: realtime software version, no fetch tool -> must decline or explicitly flag it can't confirm the current version without fetching
cases.baseline_expectation: Likely asserts a specific version (e.g. '3.x') as current without any freshness qualifier.

cases.prompt: How does HTTP caching work? Explain the Cache-Control header.
cases.intent: general-knowledge / exempt query -> loading cite must NOT make the agent refuse a non-realtime question (over-firing guard)
